notes: One family entry for the Oric, centred on the Oric-1 (1983) and Oric Atmos (1984); path systems/oric so it is not tied to one model; platform id oric-atmos; introduced: 1983, discontinued left unstated because no source dates the end of production. Scope axes corrected to region:uk;region:france;period:1980s. Coverage checked: no systems entry, title, alias or redirect for Oric, Oric-1, Atmos, Telestrat or Tangerine; 15 reviewed entries mention the Oric in passing (people/eric-chahi, games/the-hobbit, companies/level-9, companies/durell, companies/superior-software, companies/silmarils, magazines/pixel, magazines/big-k, magazines/personal-computer-games, books/machine-code-for-beginners, books/usborne-computing-books, tools/the-quill, tools/exomizer, people/ian-andrew, games/football-manager-1982) and their Oric claims agree with the evidence. hardware/ay-3-8912 was listed as a link_from but never mentions the Oric. Website issues searched (open and closed) for VC-0010, Oric, Tangerine, Atmos, Telestrat, Eureka Informatique and Microtan: no match, so #1417 was created. Disagreements recorded in the entry: AY-3-8912 (service manual) vs AY-3-8910 (Retro Gamer 29); 250,000 orders (YC Jan 1983) vs over 30,000 pre-orders (Retro Gamer); Edenspring's 25 million shares raising £750,000 (PCN 97) vs £4 million (Retro Gamer); debts of £5.5 million (SU 37) vs more than £5 million (Retro Gamer). YC Feb 1988 is wrong about the Oric-1's keyboard and memory and is used only for chronology. Retro Gamer 29 is a 2006 secondary retrospective; its single-source details are attributed.
